critical_steps: Replace g by t g in the published inequality.
Divide by t and let t tend to infinity, eliminating the gamma term.
Set g=f and use the two triangle inequalities to obtain the exact multiplicative lower and upper bounds.
One-point scalar systems attain both factors exactly.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact homogeneity argument plus one-point scalar extremizers.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made about perturbation models with normalized or otherwise constrained test vectors.

limitations: The correction applies to Theorem 4.1 under its literal universal quantification over the test vector g.
A differently normalized perturbation hypothesis could retain a meaningful K-dependent additive term.
Sharpness is for universal constants determined by the theorem's stated parameters and hypothesis.

title: The \(K\)-directed perturbation parameter is vacuous under the published quantifiers
